title: Modifier 95: Telehealth Billing Rules for 2026
summary: Modifier 95 marks live video telehealth. Medicare pairs it with POS 02 or 10, uses 93 for audio only, and limits GT. Codes, rates and denial fixes.
body_markdown:
Modifier 95 marks a service as delivered by live audio and video. On a Medicare claim it goes on the telehealth line together with place of service 02 or 10. A session held by phone only takes modifier 93 instead.


The modifier does not change what Medicare pays. The place of service code does: POS 10 pays the non facility rate and POS 02 the facility rate. For a 60 minute 90837 in 2026 that is USD 167.00 against USD 135.27 nationally.

## What is modifier 95?


Medicare contractor[Noridian](https://med.noridianmedicare.com/web/jeb/topics/modifiers/95) prints the CPT descriptor: "synchronous telemedicine service rendered via a real-time interactive audio and video telecommunications system." Noridian's instruction is one line: "Append this modifier when performing telemedicine services using real-time audio and video communications."


Synchronous means the patient and the clinician are connected at the same moment. A recorded message reviewed later is asynchronous and does not qualify. A phone call is synchronous but has no video, which is why Medicare gives it its own modifier.


### Modifier 95 at a glance


Modifier 95


Means Live, two way audio and video


Medicare pairing POS 02 or POS 10 on the same line


Audio only Use 93, not 95


Effect on Medicare payment None. The POS code sets the rate


Where it goes Each claim line delivered by video


Still valid in 2026 Yes, CMS manual chapter 26, revised May 2026


## How do you use modifier 95 on Medicare claims?


Chapter 26 of the[Medicare Claims Processing Manual](https://www.cms.gov/Regulations-and-Guidance/Guidance/Manuals/downloads/clm104c26pdf.pdf) sets the rule. Under it, POS 02 or POS 10 "must be paired with the appropriate telehealth modifier (modifier 93 for audio-only and modifier 95 for audio/video)." The same paragraph says the choice of 93 or 95 "does not change rate of payment, only the POS code determines the non-facility or facility payment rate."


CMS put that wording in with[Transmittal 12671](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/r12671cp.pdf) in June 2024, effective for services from January 1, 2024. The current chapter, revision 14466 issued May 27, 2026, still carries it word for word.


Pick the POS from where the patient is, then the modifier from the technology used:


Patient is Video and audio Audio only 2026 rate basis


At home POS 10 + modifier 95 POS 10 + modifier 93 Non facility


Somewhere other than home POS 02 + modifier 95 POS 02 + modifier 93 Facility


The rate gap is real money on time based codes. National 2026 amounts from the[CMS relative value file](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-schedules/physician/pfs-relative-value-files) , before locality adjustment:


Code POS 10 (non facility) POS 02 (facility)


90834, psychotherapy 45 min USD 113.90 USD 91.85


90837, psychotherapy 60 min USD 167.00 USD 135.27


90838, psychotherapy add-on 60 min USD 136.61 USD 110.22


99214, E/M visit, moderate USD 135.61 USD 84.50


Our[place of service codes guide](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/place-of-service-codes) covers how to confirm the patient's location before the visit.


## Modifier 95 or 93: video or audio only?


Use 95 when the session had live video for the whole service. Use 93 when it was audio only. The[CMS telehealth booklet](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/mln901705-telehealth-remote-monitoring.pdf) (MLN901705, December 2025) allows audio only for behavioral and mental health telehealth when the patient is at home.


When a video visit drops to a phone call partway through, document when it switched and why, and code by what actually happened. Payers differ on how to code a visit that switched partway, so read the payer's audio only rule first.


## Is the GT modifier still used?


For Medicare, only in one case. It applies to distant site practitioners who bill under the critical access hospital optional payment Method II. The CMS booklet says they "must submit institutional claims using the GT modifier." Professional claims from a clinic or practice use POS 02 or 10 with 95 or 93.


GQ, asynchronous store and forward, is paid only for federal telemedicine demonstrations in Alaska and Hawaii. A behavioral health group outside those programs has no use for it on Medicare claims. Some Medicaid and commercial plans kept GT in their own policies, so a payer can still ask for it.


Modifier Meaning Medicare use in 2026


95 Live audio and video With POS 02 or 10 on professional claims


93 Audio only With POS 02 or 10; behavioral health patient at home


GT Interactive audio and video (older code) CAH Method II institutional claims only


GQ Asynchronous Alaska and Hawaii demonstrations only


## Which behavioral health codes take modifier 95?


Any code on the[CY 2026 Medicare telehealth list](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/telehealth/list-services) that you deliver by video. The common behavioral health codes are all on it:


Code Service Our guide


90791, 90792 Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation


90832, 90834, 90837 Psychotherapy, 30, 45 and 60 minutes[90832](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90832-cpt-code) ,[90834](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90834-cpt-code) ,[90837](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90837-cpt-code)


90833, 90836, 90838 Psychotherapy add-ons with an E/M visit[90833](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90833-cpt-code) ,[90836](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90836-cpt-code)


90785 Interactive complexity add-on


90839, 90840 Crisis psychotherapy[90839](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90839-cpt-code)


90846, 90847 Family psychotherapy[90846](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90846-cpt-code) ,[90847](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90847-cpt-code)


90853 Group psychotherapy[90853](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90853-cpt-code)


99213, 99214 Established patient E/M visits


Modifiers sit on each claim line. An E/M visit with a psychotherapy add-on by video is two lines, for example 99214 and 90836. Each line delivered by video carries POS 10 or 02 and modifier 95. An add-on line without it does not tell the payer that part of the visit was telehealth.


When a line needs modifier 25 as well, list 25 first and 95 after it. Modifier 95 does not change Medicare payment, so it sits after modifiers that affect payment or processing. Check your contractor's own sequencing guidance, since it is the one that reads the claim.


## What should the note say for a video visit?


The note has to support every part of the claim line: the code, the place of service and the modifier. For a telehealth visit that means a few lines an in person note does not need.


What to record for every telehealth visit


- **Technology:** live video and audio for the full service, or the minute it moved to audio only and why.
- **Patient location:** home or another named place. This sets POS 10 or 02.
- **Clinician location:** where you were during the visit, for payers and state licensure rules that ask.
- **Time:** start and end, for time based codes like 90832 to 90838.
- **Consent:** that the patient agreed to telehealth, where the payer or state requires it.


The[CMS booklet](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/mln901705-telehealth-remote-monitoring.pdf) also lists an in-person rule for Medicare behavioral health telehealth. The patient needs a visit in person within 6 months of the first telehealth visit and every year after, with exceptions in 42 CFR 410.78. Congress has pushed back the start of this rule more than once. Check the[CMS telehealth page](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/telehealth) for the date in force before you build it into scheduling.

## Do Medicaid and commercial payers follow the same rules?


Not always. The Medicare manual binds Medicare contractors. Medicaid programs and commercial plans publish their own telehealth policies. They differ on whether they take POS 10, which modifier they want (95, GT or none) and whether they pay for audio only. Medicare Advantage plans can also set their own claim rules.


Keep one row per payer and update it when a policy changes:

## Why do modifier 95 claims get denied?


These mismatches send telehealth claims back. Each is a gap between the claim line and the visit, or between the claim and the payer's policy:


What went out Fix


Video visit billed with no modifier Add 95 to each line delivered by video


Phone only visit billed with 95 Use 93, or the payer's audio only code


POS 11 on a telehealth visit Use POS 10 for home, POS 02 elsewhere, for Medicare


POS 02 for a patient at home Use POS 10; it also pays the non facility rate


GT on a Medicare professional claim Use 95 or 93; GT is for CAH Method II only


Code not on the payer's telehealth list Check the list before you schedule by video


Add-on line missing the modifier Put the modifier on the add-on line too

## Modifier 95 FAQ


What is modifier 95?


A CPT modifier for a synchronous telemedicine service delivered by real-time audio and video.


Is modifier 95 still valid in 2026?


Yes. The Medicare manual, chapter 26, revised May 27, 2026, pairs POS 02 or 10 with modifier 95 for video and 93 for audio only.


Does modifier 95 change Medicare payment?


No. CMS says the place of service code sets the rate: POS 10 pays non facility, POS 02 pays facility.


Can you bill 99214 with modifier 95?


Yes. 99214 is on the CY 2026 Medicare telehealth list. Bill it with POS 10 or 02 and modifier 95 when the visit used live video.


What does modifier 95 mean on 99213?


That the 99213 visit was delivered by live audio and video.


Which goes first, modifier 25 or 95?


List 25 first, then 95. Modifier 95 does not change Medicare payment. Check your contractor's sequencing guidance.


What is the difference between modifier 95 and GT?


95 is used on Medicare professional claims with POS 02 or 10. Medicare limits GT to critical access hospital Method II institutional claims. Some other payers still ask for GT.


What modifier is used for audio only telehealth?


Modifier 93 on Medicare claims. Behavioral health audio only visits need the patient at home.
